NgraceChangeDesignContext.Rationale:
Survey of what the grammar affords today, and why this bundle specifies CloseEvidence as a child of AC-* evaluated by gate verdict on an applied archived bundle.
Afforded today. Mapped: an AC-* the plan Satisfies-links to a task. Unmapped: an AC-* with no Satisfies, warned at change.acceptance-criterion-unmapped (src/artifact/grammar.ts:1883-1890). Legacy: free-text AcceptanceCriteria with no AC-*, mapping skipped. Satisfies accepts only AC-* or None. Verdicts accept outcome pass, fail, or unable-to-determine, and optional scope task, wave, or bundle. They do not name an AC-*. Anchors may not appear in attributes.
Not afforded. No close-bound, verdict-bound, or archive-only AC-* state. No Satisfies target that is the close. No Verdict child that cites an AC-*. D17 freezes an id once a run event cites it; it does not bind a criterion to the close.
Where the evidence exists. D20 close is argv token assertions final, review, gate verdict, gate apply, gate archive, applied writes, archive move. Post-archive lint is practice after the last of those. F86: the ledger ends at the archive Decision. So the canonical 0/0 observation is after the last recording act the product already performs in the normal close.
What still records. resolveChangeBundle (src/grace-cursor.ts:500-502) finds archive/. gate verdict can write a second Verdict after the move. That is the first point where post-archive evidence can exist and a verdict can still be recorded. The writer exists; the obligation and the evaluator do not.
Why not evaluate in lint. A lint diagnostic that the close-bound criterion has not been evaluated would fire on the first post-archive lint, which is the evidence the criterion names. That is F83.1 again. Review findings are not lint issues. Gate verdict running the Command is the evaluator; review detecting a missing record is the skip detector.
Why this is smaller than the name and still the charter. The bundle does not add a post-archive lint verb or a lifecycle finish. It makes the third state real, stops the unmapped self-trap, and evaluates at a writer that already exists. Post-archive 0/0 becomes authorable as CloseEvidence whose Command is lint with argv token fail-on set to warnings. Until that ships, this bundle itself still uses the C-DRIFT-HONESTY split.
F89. A CloseEvidence tag with no Command and no evaluator would be a decoration authors could use to claim close evidence. Incomplete CloseEvidence is an error. Evaluation is gate verdict. Absence of the record is a review finding on applied archives only. If either half is cut, the state is F89 prose.

Alternatives.Alternative: Attribute on AC-* (when=close). Rejected. Semantic anchors are attribute-free. artifact.semantic-anchor-attribute and F38 already record the cost of stuffing an anchor into an attribute. when=close is not itself an anchor value, but it still violates the attribute-free rule and is only typing something (ruling 1).

Distinct sibling of AcceptanceCriteria, or a CloseSatisfies section on the plan. Rejected. The criterion is still an AC-*. Splitting the section invents a second list collectAcceptanceCriteriaIds would have to union, and plan new would still need to know which list is which.

Satisfies targeting the close or a Verdict. Rejected. Satisfies is task to AC-* (src/artifact/grammar.ts:2056-2068). A non-AC-* child is already change.plan-invalid-section-shape. The close is not a task.

Keep the C-DRIFT-HONESTY workaround as the product. Rejected as the only state. It remains the construction this bundle must use for its own 0/0 bar, but the registry charter is to make the third state authorable. A spec that only restates the workaround pays nothing.

Evaluate at argv token assertions final or at the first gate verdict. Rejected for the canonical case. Those run before the archive move. Status writes and the move can change lint (active vs archive checks). Pre-archive 0/0 is a different claim.

Require MaxErrors and MaxWarnings children and parse lint text. Deferred. Extra parser surface. Exit 0 plus fail-on warnings already expresses 0/0 with shipped CLI. Revisit if a close-bound Command is not process-exit shaped.
Raise unmapped to error. Rejected. See spec Constraints. The self-trap dies when the third state exists; the raise is not required and would break in-progress mapping.

DeferredDecisions.Decision: Whether P3.1 lifecycle finish should absorb the post-archive gate verdict so the authority does not have to remember a second verdict write. Out of this bundle. Named so C-ARCHIVE-CURSOR / D1 do not have to rediscover it.
Whether a later measurement wants Require bounds parsed from lint text instead of fail-on warnings. Not needed to ship the state.

Scenarios.Scenario: Author declares CloseEvidence with a Command that is lint plus fail-on warnings. Plan does not Satisfies it. Tasks complete. Authority runs the D20 close, moves the bundle, runs that Command via gate verdict. Verdict children record pass. Later review is quiet. Forgotten AC-* in the same spec still warns.
Author forgets to map an ordinary AC-*. Warning fires. Adding an empty CloseEvidence does not silence it; that is an error.
Author Satisfies-links a CloseEvidence AC-* because plan new used to do that. After this lands, plan new does not. If they do it by hand, both-states errors.
Bundle is superseded or cancelled. CloseEvidence is inert. No close evaluation is owed.
Authority archives and skips the post-archive verdict. Review on the applied archive finds the absence. Lint stays free of that finding, so a 0/0 Command is still runnable.
